items.title: CRS Physiology · Lecture 6: Hemodynamics
items.text: 30 questions on flow, pressure and resistance: Poiseuille's law, series vs parallel, turbulence, velocity, compliance, pulse pressure and MAP. Includes AnKing and UWorld chips and new NBME questions.

items.title: CRS Biochemistry · Lecture 5: Eicosanoid Metabolism
items.text: 29 questions on prostaglandins, thromboxanes and leukotrienes, the COX and lipoxygenase pathways and the drugs that block them, plus Dr. Shetty's 2 practice questions. Includes AnKing and UWorld chips and new NBME questions.

items.title: NBME study guides
items.text: New Hemodynamics and Eicosanoids sections in the CRS Physiology and Biochemistry guides.

items.title: Incorrect questions per lecture
items.text: Each lecture now has an ✗ Incorrect tile that opens only the questions you missed in that lecture.

items.title: Tidier lecture chips
items.text: The lecture chips are now a compact 2-row tile grid: Easy, Hard and Incorrect on top, then professor questions, AnKing and UWorld.

items.title: CRS Embryology · Lecture 4
items.text: Now only covers what was taught: the arterial (aortic) arches and arteries, 27 questions. Fetal circulation and vein questions are still in All CRS Embryology.

items.title: Cardiac cycle & PV loop
items.text: Every condition re-checked. ↑ Preload widens the loop with ESV unchanged, exercise now raises stroke volume, aortic stenosis shows a slow aortic rise, and the T wave ends at S2.

items.title: Class stats sooner
items.text: The class percent correct now shows on a question as soon as one classmate has answered it.

items.title: Heart Development 3D: aortic arches
items.text: 4 new stages: the arch arteries, carotids and aortic arch, pulmonary arteries with the ductus and recurrent laryngeal nerves, and the dorsal aorta's branches.

items.title: Clearer 3D labels
items.text: Labels now sit at the sides with pointer lines, so they never cover the model.

items.title: Faster refresh
items.text: Refreshing takes you straight back to where you were, without the sign-in screen.

items.title: Google sign-in on iPhones
items.text: Sign-in now works on iPhones and when the link is opened inside apps like WhatsApp or Instagram.

items.title: CRS Biochem · Lecture 4: Complex Lipid Metabolism
items.text: 26 questions, Dr. Shetty's 3 practice Q's, AnKing and UWorld chips, 9 NBME questions and a new study guide section.

items.title: Ethics tab rebuilt
items.text: All 102 Windsor ethics review questions in the USMLE question view, sorted into 21 topics.

items.title: Update button
items.text: You'll get a refresh button when a new version is out, and this summary after you refresh.
